solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Extra wealthy person keeping everyone under

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed under another follows it in the answer

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a rich or upper-class person
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A rich man is keeping everybody beneath him as a spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' just joins; 'under' puts ALL below NOB in the column. A NO-BALL is an illegal delivery in cricket that gives the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a no-ball concedes a penalty run, one of the so-called extras.

clue.text: I'm loyal, party having got involved in a bit of old-fashioned drama

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loyal party member describes getting caught up in some old-fashioned theatrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having got involved' rearranges the letters of I'M LOYAL PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval allegorical plays teaching virtue were a dramatic form now long out of fashion.

clue.text: Beggar's confession about inability to put things right?

parts.note: to put things right is to repair them, to mend
the admission I CAN'T confesses one is unable

explanation.surface: A beggar admits he is unable to fix anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mend? I can't' as a confession of being unable to put things right; the 's after Beggar is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant is someone living by asking for alms, a begging friar or pauper.

clue.text: Dismissed a Parisian in the course of disturbance

indicators.note: something occurring in the course of a thing lies inside it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a rout is a disorderly crowd or tumult
UN is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Someone from Paris got thrown out during a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN OUT is a way for a batsman to be dismissed in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket batsman is run out when the bails are broken before he regains his ground, so he is out.

clue.text: Even temper that's necessary for one learning deportment with books aloft!

definitions.text: that's necessary for one learning deportment with books aloft!
definitions.meaning: pupils practising good posture walk with books balanced on their heads, needing a literally level head

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: a head held level so books on it don't fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sensible and composed under pressure is the calm disposition called an even temper.

clue.text: Gate there dangling — not entirely fixed

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, so the letters are found within them

explanation.surface: A gate swinging loose is only partly secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' points to the letters inside gaTE THERE Dangling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tied down with a rope is fastened in place, secured.

clue.text: One in secret scheme who will get things off the ground?

definitions.text: who will get things off the ground?

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: a plot is a secret plan
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A conspirator in a secret plan is the one who will launch the project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get things off the ground' sounds like starting a project but means flying an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies aircraft, literally lifting them off the ground, and also leads trial schemes.

clue.text: Bizarre idea about cold metal being radioactive element

indicators.note: the reworked letters go around the other pieces
a bizarre version of the word is a strange rearrangement of it

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A strange notion concerning a cold metal turning out to be radioactive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bizarre' rearranges the fodder into a shape that splits around the inserted pieces, which 'about' signals; 'being' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The actinides are a series of heavy radioactive elements such as uranium and plutonium.

clue.text: Black mineral in hole

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as in pencil grades
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Dark mineral is found down a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore is a hole drilled out, as for a well or the inside of a gun barrel.

clue.text: Very small country — it has hidden energy

parts.note: V is the small, abbreviated form of very

indicators.note: a country that has something hidden contains it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: Italy is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny nation has secret reserves of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has hidden' puts the pronoun inside the country's name near its end. Italy is hardly small, so 'small' is best read as describing the abbreviation for very.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitality is liveliness and vigour, a person's store of energy.

clue.text: Offensive doctor given medal — one kept in bedroom?

parts.note: an offensive is a military attack, war
the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An aggressive doctor receives an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective but is a noun for an attack. The OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is the tall cupboard where clothes are stored in a bedroom.

clue.text: Amount of temporary accommodation given to old lover

indicators.note: the shelter is handed over to the former partner, so they are joined, the ex in front

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: How much camping gear was handed to a former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the size, scope or degree of something, its amount.

clue.text: Bird or spider unfortunate old woman swallowed?

definitions.meaning: a small bird that catches insects in flight
in the nursery rhyme the old lady swallowed a spider to catch the fly she had swallowed

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'There Was an Old Lady Who Swallowed a Fly' has her swallow a spider to catch the fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a songbird family named for snatching insects mid-air; the spider is a catcher of flies.

clue.text: Makes improvements to this writer in final bits

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: the final bits of something are its ends
the setter calls himself me

explanation.surface: An author tidies up the last pieces of a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct it, improving its wording.

clue.text: Performer in river, wounded worker

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
cut means wounded
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: An injured labourer is found in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is the river that flows through Exeter in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An executant is one who carries out a performance, particularly a musician.

clue.text: Stick out for short time, discourteous to others

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
T is the abbreviation for time
rude means impolite to people

explanation.surface: Briefly be noticeable, being impolite to everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to jut out beyond a surface, extend outward.

clue.text: Vegetable supplied by place in Somerset

definitions.meaning: A market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England

explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leaf beet eaten as greens; Chard is also a Somerset town.

clue.text: Cooking a couple of fish by the sound of it

indicators.note: the words are said aloud and heard as another word

parts.note: cod and ling are two fish, together a cod-ling

explanation.surface: Preparing two fish, judging by what you hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod and ling run together sound like the cooking term; coddling is gently simmering, as in a coddled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle eggs is to cook them gently in water just below boiling.

clue.text: Greek and German meeting in cave

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A Greek and a German get together in a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave or cavern.

clue.text: Cope with duress somehow in legal administration

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Handle coercion in some fashion when running the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges COPE and DURESS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Due process is the fair application of established legal procedure.

clue.text: Queen of island beset by mounting fury

indicators.note: the island is surrounded by the other letters
in a down clue mounting means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: fury means anger

explanation.surface: A queen of an island is besieged by rising rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns ANGER into REGNA; 'beset by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, used in the monarch's official signature.

clue.text: Taste that's acidic getting Virginia upset inside

indicators.note: the turned piece goes inside the other

parts.note: acidic means sour

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A sharp flavour that has Virginia feeling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the state abbreviation round before 'inside' places it within the sharp-tasting word; 'that's' and 'getting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour is to taste and enjoy; as a noun it is a characteristic flavour.

clue.text: Holy person got old and performed publicly?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
aged means grew old

explanation.surface: A saint grew old and made public appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged play is put on for an audience, presented in public.

clue.text: Bit of time soldier's taken over making device

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldier piece is taken over, placed above, the time piece

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier, and the 's gives the S
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: A soldier's short break is spent making a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'taken over' sets the soldiers above the moment. 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gismo or gizmo is a gadget, an ingenious mechanical contrivance.

clue.text: Pessimistic resident has limited say

indicators.note: the resident holds the other letters within bounds, enclosing them

parts.note: a native is a local inhabitant
EG, for example, is what say means as in say ten

explanation.surface: A local person's opinion is restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has limited' means the resident encloses 'say', the usual crossword stand-in for for example, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative attitude is one that dwells on the downside, gloomy and doubtful.

clue.text: One hut is constructed for dwarf

indicators.note: something constructed is built from parts, so the letters are put together anew

explanation.surface: A single shed is built for a small person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dwarf' looks like a noun but is a verb: to overshadow. 'constructed' rearranges ONE HUT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwarf something is to surpass it so it seems small, excelling over it.

clue.text: We in Calais must show common sense

definitions.meaning: the French word for we, as used in a French town
practical intelligence, a British informal word from Greek

explanation.definitionFit: The French pronoun for we is spelt this way, and British slang uses it for practical wit.

clue.text: Dances — ten got nasty sort of drug

indicators.note: a nasty turn of events leaves things messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Dancing turned unpleasant after some type of pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges DANCES, TEN and GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A decongestant is a medicine that relieves a blocked nose.
